newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina probing $800 mln squid fraud.
newsitem.headline: Argentina probing $800 mln squid fraud.

text.p: Argentine courts are investigating a possible $800 million fraud by fishing companies which allegedly made false claims for squid export rebates, a legal official said Thursday.
Prosecutor Raul Plee ordered the arrests of officials from 20 Argentine fishing companies for the fraud allegedly committed between 1993 and 1996, an official at his office told Reuters.
The firms allegedly claimed export rebates for squid while allowing boats from Japan, Taiwan and South Korea to operate using their fishing licenses in the Argentine South Atlantic.
Plee also ordered the arrest of a senior customs official at the Patagonian port of Santa Cruz.

The scale of the alleged squid fraud against Argentina's cash-strapped public finances invites comparison with a probe into a smuggling ring within the customs service which the government thinks cost it $3 billion over four years.
